case.court_name: Court of Appeal of Sri Lanka

clause.text: Any accused person has the right to a fair trial and legal representation.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the appellant, charged with contempt of court for giving false evidence, was deprived of the right to a fair trial and legal representation under Article 13(3) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The appellant argued that he was not given an opportunity to answer the charge properly and was denied legal representation, violating his constitutional right to a fair trial under Article 13(3).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondent did not explicitly contest the constitutional claim but relied on the procedure under Section 449(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure to summarily convict the appellant for contempt of court.
key_facts: The appellant was the first prosecution witness and was treated as an adverse witness during the main trial.
The trial judge convicted the appellant for contempt of court on the same day after his evidence without giving reasons for the sentence.
The appellant was not given a proper opportunity to explain or deny the charge of giving false evidence.
The appellant was not afforded legal representation during the contempt proceedings.
The trial judge failed to record reasons for imposing the sentence as required by law.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 13(3) as guaranteeing the right of any accused person to a fair trial, which includes the right to be heard and to have legal representation. This right extends to a witness charged with contempt of court for giving false evidence during a High Court trial.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the appellant was deprived of the opportunity to properly answer the charge and was denied legal representation, violating the constitutional guarantee of a fair trial. The trial judge's failure to give reasons for the sentence further compounded the unfairness.
principles_established: A witness charged with contempt of court in a High Court trial is entitled to legal representation.
The accused must be given an opportunity to explain or deny the charge before conviction.
The trial judge must record reasons for imposing a sentence under Section 449(1).
precedents_cited: Chang Han King vs Piggott (1909) AC 312
Subramaniam vs Queen (1868) 5 Moore NS 11116 ER 457
Muttusamy vs Attorney General SC Application 81/94
Tillekeratne vs Officer in Charge Pugoda Police Station [1997] 1 Sri.L.R.

outcome.holding: The court held that the appellant's constitutional right under Article 13(3) was violated as he was denied a fair trial and legal representation. The conviction and sentence were set aside and the appellant was acquitted.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Conviction and sentence set aside; appellant acquitted.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(3) was central to the court's reasoning because it guarantees the right to a fair trial and legal representation, which the appellant was denied during the contempt proceedings. The violation of this right led to the setting aside of the conviction.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The appellant was not given an opportunity to answer the charge properly and was denied legal representation, violating Article 13(3). The trial judge also failed to give reasons for the sentence as required by law.
